finding.text: `quiet_follow` skips the whole of `wake_parent`, not only the message to the parent (Servex/agents/Agents.js, the `emit` hunk near line 1779). So `this.inbox(child, …)` and the "Next: … start it" note for landed tasks (Agents.js:988-989) are skipped too. Example: a mastermind's turn is started by a followed "complete" line, it merges, lands its task and replies "Merged, landed." (under 200 chars). Its parent never hears about it, the inbox records nothing, and the queued sibling never starts. Skip only the `send`, and still wake when `child.task?.dir` has landed.

Nobody can continue from this task folder. It has no `requirements.md`; the brief is one sentence in `task.jsonl` line 1, and the owner's words (session-smart-v-sq8y7db) are not quoted or linked. That `task.jsonl` exists only on `worktree/queue-landed-drop`, and its `now` is still "landing" with no `landed_at` line.
The new task folder is not in its parent's record. `dictation-debug/session.jsonl` has no line naming `queue-and-follow`, in the main tree or in the worktree (Law 10: index everything you create).

The follow change has no test. `Servex/Gate-stale.test.mjs` covers only `stale`; nothing checks that a short ack after followed lines doesn't wake the parent, or that a long answer, `BLOCKED` or a mixed queue still does. Follow-kind and Follow-skip set the pattern: add a `Follow-ack.test.mjs` and name it in Servex/doc/follow.md's new section.

`follow_only` is reset to `undefined` at every result (Agents.js, the `emit` hunk), so it forgets a non-follow message that is already queued. Example: a followed turn F is running and the parent's question M is queued. F's result resets the flag. A followed line G then arrives while M runs and sets it to true, so M's short answer ("yes") is swallowed. To fix it, count pending non-follow turns instead of keeping one flag.

Gate-stale stubs `agents.blocked`, so it proves only that `stale` passes `landed: false`. It never runs the real `task_dir_for` fallbacks (`task_dir_of`, `find_task_dir`), which are what matched the old `ai-system-mastermind` task. It passes: `node Servex/Gate-stale.test.mjs` printed "Gate-stale: ok" in the worktree.

The 200-character limit is a fixed number, and only follow.md mentions it. A follower writing a short answer it wants the parent to see has no way to know it will be dropped. One line in the roles that follow logs ("news goes through send_to_agent") would close that gap.

`turn_kinds` drifts out of step with the turns, because only `Agent.send` pushes onto it. The first prompt (Servex/agents/Agents.js:1239) and `/compact` (Agents.js:1596) start turns with no entry, and an idle stop's `result` still shifts one (Agents.js:1780). Example: a mastermind is spawned with its brief and told to `follow` the seat's file, so a followed line arrives while the brief's turn is still running. The brief's turn then reads that line's `true`, its short reply ("Spawned the minion, watching") wakes nobody, and every later turn reads the entry of the message before it. To fix it, push an entry wherever a turn is queued (`false` at 1239 and 1596), and shift only when a turn actually ran.

Round 1's finding 3 is still open. `dictation-debug/session.jsonl` has no line naming `queue-and-follow` (`grep -c` gives 0 in the worktree), so the task folder is not in its parent's record (Law 10).

Round 1's finding 1 is fixed: with `quiet`, `wake_parent` still writes the inbox and still sends the "Next:" note (Agents.js:991-992). Finding 4 is fixed too: `Servex/agents/Follow-ack.test.mjs` covers a short ack, a long answer, BLOCKED, a real message, and a real message queued behind a followed line, and follow.md names the test. Both tests print ok in the worktree.

Follow-ack.test.mjs never starts a turn from the first prompt or from `/compact`, so the drift in finding 1 passes the test. Add a test that spawns with a `prompt`, sends a followed line, then emits two results.

The test assumes one SDK `result` per queued user message. If the SDK ever folds two queued messages into one turn, the list drifts the same way, so a count kept per turn would be safer than a list shifted once per result.
task.jsonl (worktree) still says `now: "landing"` and has no `landed_at` line. That is expected before the merge, but the task must still land when it is merged.

A real question's short answer can still be swallowed (Servex/agents/Agents.js:1780-1781, worktree head b4dbfc62e). The counters reset at every result, so with a followed turn F running and the parent's question M queued, F's result zeroes both counts; a followed line G that arrives while M runs then makes M's turn look "followed only", and M's answer "yes" wakes nobody. This is round 1's note 5 come back with counters; keep the count per queued turn (push a kind when a turn is queued, shift it when its result arrives) and add this exact case to Follow-ack.test.mjs, which today checks a mix only when both messages land before the first result (lines 137-143).

The `/compact` turn (Agents.js:1596) is not counted. A followed line that arrives during it makes the compact's own result "quiet" (harmless), but the counts are then 0 when the followed line's own turn ends, so that ack wakes the parent after all. Counting per queued turn (finding 1) fixes this too.

Round 2's index finding is fixed: dictation-debug/session.jsonl:218 names the task folder and its branch. Both tests print ok in the worktree (`node Servex/agents/Follow-ack.test.mjs`, `node Servex/Gate-stale.test.mjs`).

Ask 1 asks for "stays queued … or the parent is told and it re-queues". The fix removes the wrong drop and tells the parent, but a drop does not re-queue; the parent must spawn again (Servex/Servex.js:1306). Fine given the real cause, but requirements.md should say re-queue was not built and why.

task.jsonl's three lines are stamped `2026-10-25T20:00:00-07:00`, a made-up time in the wrong zone (every other line in this folder is -05:00, around 17:50). It still says `now: "landing"` with no `landed_at`, which must be closed when it merges.

This task's record is in two places, and they disagree, so the merge will stop. The main tree has an untracked `queue-and-follow/task.jsonl` holding three review rounds, the answers and a "Landed:" log line. The branch adds its own `task.jsonl` at the same path (diff.patch, last hunk), so `git merge worktree/queue-landed-drop` will refuse to overwrite the untracked file. Join the two into one file (the branch's assign line first, then the review lines), then add a real `landed_at` line; neither copy has one, and the branch copy still says `now: "landing"`.

Round 3's fix finding is resolved at head 5d5988b3a. Each queue push records its own kind (`AgentQueue.push`, Servex/agents/Agents.js:2377), and each result shifts one kind (Agents.js:1780). The first prompt, `/compact` and held replays all go through `push`, so they count too. Follow-ack.test.mjs now tests the exact swallowed-answer case (followed F, question M queued behind it, followed G arriving during M). `node Servex/agents/Follow-ack.test.mjs` and `node Servex/Gate-stale.test.mjs` both print ok in the worktree.

The list assumes one SDK `result` per queued message. A `priority: "now"` message relies on the measured "the running turn ends with a null result" (Agents.js:1448-1451). If that null result doesn't come through `emit` as a `result`, the list slips by one. Servex/doc/follow.md:180 states the general limit; it could name the `now` case too.

When `awaken` runs, `start()` makes a new queue (Agents.js:1213), so `kinds` restarts empty. Any result still arriving from the old process would shift the new list. This is unlikely, but nothing tests it.

The three lines in the branch's task.jsonl are still stamped `2026-10-25T20:00:00-07:00`, a made-up time. A later line in the main tree's copy admits this, but the fix in 1 is the moment to correct them.

Requirements are met. Ask 1: the drop came from a wrong "landed" match, not from a RAM timeout; that match is fixed (Servex/Servex.js:1304), and a drop now tells the parent. requirements.md's "Not built" section explains why there is no automatic re-queue. Ask 2: the cause is named (`wake_parent`), short acks are now quiet, and session-smart.md:50 tells followers to send news with `send_to_agent`. The docs are current: dormant.md:131 and follow.md:178 each name their test. The parent index is in michael/dev's dictation-debug/session.jsonl.

The task record `queue-and-follow/task.jsonl` lives only in the main tree and is untracked (`git ls-files` does not know it), with `now: "merging"` and no `landed_at` line. The branch no longer adds a copy (diff.patch has no task.jsonl hunk), so last round's merge clash is gone. The landing step still has to write `landed_at` and commit this file, or the record is lost.

The doc comment above `Agents.blocked` (Servex/agents/Agents.js:634) names only the boot sweep as a caller that passes `landed: false`. `Servex.stale` (Servex/Servex.js:1304) now passes it too, whenever the spec names no task dir. One clause there would keep the comment true.

The `kinds` list is shifted only on `result` events (Agents.js:1779). A turn that ends with an `error` event and no `result` would leave its entry behind, and every later turn would then be judged one off. follow.md:200 covers the merged-turn, `priority: "now"` and awaken cases, but not this one.

Requirements are met. Ask 1: there was no RAM timeout. The real cause was a wrong "landed" match, now fixed (Servex.js:1304), and a dropped spawn now tells its parent. requirements.md's "Not built" section says why there is no automatic re-queue. Ask 2: the cause is named (`Agents.wake_parent`), short acks after a followed line no longer wake the parent (they still reach its inbox and the "Next:" note), and session-smart.md:50 tells followers to send news with `send_to_agent`. `node Servex/Gate-stale.test.mjs` and `node Servex/agents/Follow-ack.test.mjs` both print ok at worktree head b4c0c0c81.

The docs are current and the work is indexed. dormant.md:183 and follow.md:198 each name their test. requirements.md links both docs. dictation-debug/session.jsonl:218 records the task, with its branch `worktree/queue-landed-drop`. A fresh agent could pick this up from the task folder: requirements.md holds the asks, the findings and what was not built, and task.jsonl holds every review round and answer.
